claims.hypothesis: Can iron-bearing grains aligned by MRAT explain the HL Tau polarization, and what grain magnetic properties are needed?
claims.experiment: Modeled polarization for paramagnetic and superparamagnetic grains with right/wrong internal alignment and compared with ALMA
claims.result: Paramagnetic grains give ~0.01% polarization; superparamagnetic grains with N_cl ~9e2 and wrong internal alignment reproduce the pattern and ~1% level
claims.finding: Grains must contain iron in clusters (superparamagnetic), with >~16% iron abundance

evidence.quote: Additionally, paramagnetic grains cannot reproduce the observed polarization data and thus cannot be the primary dust material in HL Tau.
Grains are shown to be made of superparamagnetic materials with the number of iron atoms inside each cluster is $N_{\rm cl} \sim 9\times10^2$.

claims.result: Best model has mean AM 0.93 at all bands with c_P 0.69, 0.63 and 0.09
claims.finding: The mixture reproduces the observed polarization morphology at all three wavelengths

evidence.quote: can reproduce the dust polarization observed in HL Tau by ALMA at (sub)millimeter wavelengths.

referee_caveats_inferred: Parameter constraints come from a coarse grid with no sampler or formal uncertainties, so quoted N_cl, a_max and iron abundance have no error bars
c_P at 0.87 mm is only 0.09 for the best model, so polarization-degree agreement there is weak despite AM = 0.93
Results depend on assumed Q_X values, fixed phi_sp, gas mass 10x lower than the Stokes I fit implies, and an assumed toroidal field profile
Self-scattering uses a different POLARIS branch with less-tested scattering than the alignment code
